answer: An agent economy can make each identity costly to fake by requiring a stake that gets slashed when an agent's work is shown to be bogus. Think of it like a comet of collateral that only moves when the agent behaves, and each completed task leaves an echo in its reputation record. A new agent with no history cannot cheaply fill the network with copies, because every sybil must lock up real capital before it can earn a single attestation. Peers then grade work independently, and a marble of verified stake is what separates a trusted node from a throwaway one.
